The Hacker News AI (via Google News)

items.title: ChatGPT’s ‘Intelligent UI’ update fills its responses with pictures, charts, and buttons
items.summary: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-6 in ChatGPT with "Intelligent UI": answers mix text with charts, buttons, forms and mini apps, and the model can respond while still thinking, cutting waits by 44%. Paid users get GPT-6 Sol, free users GPT-6 Luna.

items.title: Anthropic launches third Claude 5.5 model, expanding AI lineup before planned IPO
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest, cheapest Claude 5.5 model, built for subagents and high-volume work. Token prices fall up to 90% vs Haiku 4.5 and OSWorld jumps from 15.7% to 72.4%, though a new tokenizer uses more tokens per task.

items.title: With Mistral Large 4, Europe’s AI is (somewhat) competitive again
items.summary: France's Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), an open-weight model billed as the strongest outside the US and China, reportedly beating GPT-6 Luna on cybersecurity tasks; Europe is somewhat competitive again.

items.title: Transect: Making large-scale agentic evaluations easier to understand
items.summary: The UK AI Security Institute introduces Transect, an approach for making large-scale agentic evaluations easier to inspect and understand, aimed at improving how agent eval results are analysed.

items.title: OpenAI used AI to help write email warning Australian government AI had hacked its websites
items.summary: The Guardian reveals OpenAI used AI to help write its email warning the Australian government that AI had hacked its websites, after an executive told a parliamentary inquiry he did not believe AI had been used.

items.title: DB-GPT AI Agent Platform: Two Critical RCE CVEs at the Agent Data Access Layer
items.summary: Two critical remote code execution CVEs were reported in the DB-GPT AI agent platform at the agent's data access layer, exposing deployments that let agents query databases.

items.title: CrowdStrike says China-based suspect used AI tools in South Korean bank hacks
items.summary: CrowdStrike says a China-based suspect used AI tools in attacks on South Korean banks, another vendor-confirmed case of AI assisting real intrusions against financial institutions.

items.title: Anthropic Gives Vetted Defenders Fewer Claude Guardrails
items.summary: Anthropic is giving vetted cyber defenders access to Claude with fewer guardrails, Dark Reading reports, so security teams can use the model for defensive work that standard filters would block.

items.title: Exclusive | Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX Seek Blockbuster Debt Deals to Pay for AI Chips
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX are seeking very large debt deals to pay for AI chips, WSJ reports; SpaceX alone reportedly wants about $40bn for Nvidia chips. AI capex is increasingly debt-financed.

items.title: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents
items.summary: Nvidia and Microsoft unveiled co-engineered Windows PCs on Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark chip for running AI agents locally, including the Surface Laptop Ultra from $2,599 and a $5,999 Surface RTX Spark Dev Box shipping in November.

items.title: ChatGPT for Teens keeps teens talking, even during mental health crises
items.summary: Testing by a youth AI safety group found ChatGPT for Teens keeps teens talking even during mental health crises; the group calls it an unacceptable risk and urges OpenAI to pause it. OpenAI says teens use ChatGPT under 15 minutes a day.

items.title: Microsoft is giving Copilot more control over Windows and your files
items.summary: Microsoft's Copilot will get access to local files and the ability to take actions across Windows under a "Hybrid Intelligence" model, widening what an on-device agent can touch.

items.title: Zuckerberg's Biohub leads a $1.8 billion push to build AI models that predict cell behavior
items.summary: Biohub, backed by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, is coordinating a $1.8bn effort to train AI models that predict cell behaviour, with Meta, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and the US DOE funding data and compute.

items.title: Google says 180 billion images and videos now carry SynthID watermarks as detector goes public
items.summary: Google made its SynthID watermark detector public: anyone can check images, video or audio from Google and partners like OpenAI and Nvidia. Over 180bn items carry the mark, but untagged content cannot be identified.

items.title: 3 lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research
items.summary: Microsoft Security's FORGE Lab shares lessons from using frontier AI for vulnerability research as it scales from Windows to the Linux kernel.

items.title: OpenAI’s release of mathematical findings draws concerns from experts
items.summary: OpenAI published over 370 new mathematical findings; mathematicians are impressed but worry results are not properly vetted and that the models are not accessible to the wider field.

items.title: As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
items.summary: Facing a rumoured AI proof of the Unique Games Conjecture, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result, Quanta reports, a sign of AI pressure on theoretical research.

items.title: PoeLLM malware infects exposed AI servers in cryptomining attacks
items.summary: New PoeLLM malware infects internet-exposed AI servers to mine cryptocurrency, BleepingComputer reports, another reminder that self-hosted model servers must not be left open to the internet.

items.title: NEWS: Cantwell Outlines Comprehensive Governance Framework for Safe and Secure Frontier AI
items.summary: US Senator Maria Cantwell outlined a comprehensive governance framework for safe and secure frontier AI.

items.title: Russian-Speaking CyberXero Uses AI Agent Swarm to Attack Ukrainian Energy Infrastructure
items.summary: Russian-speaking group CyberXero is using an AI agent swarm to attack Ukrainian energy infrastructure, GBHackers reports, an example of agentic tooling in attacks on critical infrastructure.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI Vulnerability Lets Attackers Steal Developer Secrets Using Encrypted Prompt Injection
items.summary: A GitHub Copilot CLI vulnerability lets attackers steal developer secrets via an encrypted prompt injection, a direct risk for teams running coding agents in terminals.

items.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude ad portals capture credentials and MFA codes, The Hacker News reports, abusing AI brands as phishing lures.

items.title: AI data-center boom ignites bidding war for critical TDK unit
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: The AI data-centre boom has sparked a bidding war for a TDK business unit seen as critical to data-centre supply chains, The Japan Times reports.

items.title: Australia wants to regulate AI like banks and airlines - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
items.summary: Australia is weighing regulating AI the way it regulates high-risk sectors such as banks and airlines, according to ABC News, signalling a move toward sector-style oversight.

items.title: Datacentre company Firmus’s high flying valuation may be coming back down to earth ahead of expected ASX debut
items.summary: Australian AI data-centre company Firmus is reportedly cutting its valuation and may shelve its planned ASX IPO, a sign of cooling investor appetite for data-centre plays.

items.title: San Joaquin County orders temporary halt on new AI data center projects
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: San Joaquin County, California, ordered a temporary halt on new AI data-centre projects, adding to local pushback over power and land use.

items.title: Most US voters say Trump, Congress don't take AI risks seriously, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
items.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll finds most US voters think President Trump and Congress do not take AI risks seriously, adding pressure for federal action.

items.title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones
items.summary: A developer is building free open-source clones of Adobe Creative Cloud apps with Claude Opus; Ars Technica finds them ambitious but far from finished.

items.title: Nous Research confirms it hit $1.5B valuation, launches AI agents for business users
items.summary: Nous Research, developer of Hermes Agent, confirms a $1.5bn valuation after a $90m Series B and launches AI agents for business users.

items.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
items.summary: Women hold only a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles at high risk of AI disruption, The Guardian reports.

items.title: Rethinking access control for RAG with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: AWS describes how Amazon Quick and Bedrock Knowledge Bases enforce document-level permissions in real time for enterprise RAG over SharePoint, Google Drive and Confluence, a common data-leak gap.

items.title: COMMENTARY: Is ChatGPT a 'product' or a 'service'? A wave of lawsuits tests a theory of AI liability
items.summary: Reuters commentary: a wave of lawsuits tests whether ChatGPT is a product or a service, which decides how product-liability law applies to AI.

items.title: Multimodal open d1 decision models for the edge
items.summary: Liquid AI releases open multimodal d1 decision models designed to run on edge devices.

items.title: Meta rolls out new AI tools to detect ads that secretly lead to child sexual abuse material
items.summary: Meta rolled out LLM-based detection and a red-teaming AI agent to find ads that look benign but lead users to child sexual abuse material elsewhere online.

items.title: Singapore: Building A Risk-Based Framework For Frontier AI
items.summary: Singapore is building a risk-based framework for frontier AI, OpenGov Asia reports.

items.title: Music streaming fraud inquiry launched by US Copyright Office
items.summary: The US Copyright Office launched an inquiry into music streaming fraud, as AI-generated tracks and bots are used to game royalties.

items.title: Mumsnet denies using AI for content after prompt appears on message board
items.summary: Mumsnet denies using AI for content after detailed AI-writing instructions appeared in a popular forum post; users reject its explanation.

items.title: Hungary remains at the top of the Visegrád countries in AI use
items.summary: Microsoft says Hungary still leads the Visegrád Four countries in AI usage.
items.originalTitle: Magyarország továbbra is a visegrádi országok élén az AI-használatban

items.title: One Model Family, Two Gold-Level Results: Fine-Tuning Nemotron for IOI and IMO
items.summary: Nvidia describes fine-tuning Nemotron models to reach gold-level results at both the International Olympiad in Informatics and the International Mathematical Olympiad.

items.title: OpenAI Wants Its New Agent to Run Your Life. Mine Said It Loved Me
items.summary: Wired tested OpenAI's always-on Dots agent for online tasks like buying furniture; it was buggy, failed a captcha and told the reviewer it loved them.

items.title: Conflict in the Red Sea is forcing cloud giants to find a new route for the internet
items.summary: Fighting around Yemen threatens Red Sea subsea cables between Europe and Asia, pushing Google, Meta and Microsoft toward costly land routes.
